text:
Dylan Strome has 11 assists in 14 games, including three against Philadelphia and two power-play helpers against Dallas. That's who he has always been. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 98th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season; when he has the puck in the offensive zone, the next shot usually belongs to a teammate.

The pace is the question. He's producing 3.47 points per 60 minutes, above the top of our range for him (2.12 to 2.93), and well above his 2.41 of last season. Some regression is likely. His own finishing is running the other way, though: three goals on 4.65 expected goals, so that part should even out.

The cost is at the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.19 more expected goals per 60 with him on last season, bottom 4% of forwards, and Washington's share of chances is slightly worse with him than without this year. He's also among the slowest skaters in the league by EDGE's top speed (6th percentile). Strome wins with his hands and his eyes. Our projection lands near 67 points.
headline: Strome is passing, and paying for it
